**Allowed origins** are decided by the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `app.use('*', cors(...))`, at `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes back the request's origin only if one of these holds:
- The origin is exactly `http://localhost:4200`.
- The origin ends with `.pages.dev`. This matches any depth, so any Cloudflare Pages site is allowed.
- The origin ends with `.workers.dev`. This also matches any depth.

Any other origin, and requests with no `Origin` header, get `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The same middleware sets:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization
- `maxAge`: 86400

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add another `||` clause, for example `origin === 'https://play.example.com'`, next to the `localhost:4200` check. Use an exact full-origin match, including the scheme and no trailing slash. Don't switch to an array of origins. The comment at line 20 and `docs/code/worker/src/index.md` explain that Hono matches array entries as exact strings, so wildcards wouldn't work there.

If you're careful, avoid a bare `endsWith('.example.com')`. It would also match something like `evil-example.com` unless the suffix starts with the dot, and it would allow every subdomain.

After the change, redeploy the Worker. Per `docs/code/worker/src/index.md`, the rationale is also covered in `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 (CORS). I didn't open that section. If you do make the edit, update the "Responsibilities" bullet in `docs/code/worker/src/index.md`, which lists the allowed origins.
